raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

context:
  version: "0.8.3"
  sha256: d43ffceb77110a18eda2dc38384e3ef77aa0acdd0fe0b6f27756a2799fdaae87
  bazel_version: "7.2.1"

package:
  name: array-record
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://github.com/google/array_record/archive/v${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: ${{ sha256 }}

build:
  number: 1
  skip:
    - match(python, "<3.11")
    - win

requirements:
  build:
    - if: target_platform != build_platform
      then:
        - python
        - pip
        - numpy
        - setuptools
        - wheel
    - bazel 7.2.1.*
    - rsync
    - ${{ compiler('c') }}
    - ${{ stdlib('c') }}
    - ${{ compiler('cxx') }}
    - if: osx
      then:
        # Why bazel-toolchain:
        # - Bazel's builtin C++ toolchain autoconfiguration reaches for the
        #   std*.h headers from the real Xcode SDK instead of the ones under
        #   CONDA_BUILD_SYSROOT.
        # - bazel-toolchain generates a crosstool from the active conda
        #   compilers, and build.sh tells bazel to use that instead.
        #
        # Why pinned <0.5:
        # - 0.5.0 ("Adjust for bazel9") made the generated BUILD files load
        #   @rules_cc//cc/toolchains and @rules_cc//cc/common.
        # - Those packages don't exist in the rules_cc version which
        #   array_record's MODULE.bazel resolves to, breaking the build with
        #   a "cc/toolchains is not a package" error.
        # - <0.5 still uses plain Bazel-builtin cc_toolchain rules under the
        #   same //bazel_toolchain:* labels, so it stays compatible.
        - bazel-toolchain <0.5
  host:
    - python
    - pip
    - numpy
    - setuptools
    - wheel
  run:
    - python
    - etils
    - absl-py
    - numpy
    - more-itertools >=9.1.0
    - typing_extensions
    - importlib_resources
    - zipp
    - fsspec

tests:
  - python:
      imports:
        - array_record
      pip_check: true
  - files:
      recipe:
        - test_array_record.py
    requirements:
      run:
        - pip
        - python
    script:
      - python test_array_record.py

about:
  summary: ArrayRecord file format.
  description: |
    ArrayRecord is a new file format derived from [Riegeli](https://github.com/google/riegeli),
    achieving a new frontier of IO efficiency. We designed ArrayRecord to support parallel
    read, write, and random access by record index. ArrayRecord builds on top of Riegeli
    and supports the same compression algorithms.
  license: Apache-2.0
  license_file: LICENSE
  homepage: https://pypi.org/project/array-record/
  repository: https://github.com/google/array-record/

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - iindyk
    - mtsokol
    - mgorny
    - pb01ka
